reason: The hypothesis relies on configurational entropy suppressing ordering, but the cited evidence (E2) explicitly shows large chemical clustering in AlxCrCoFeNi over a wide temperature range, directly contradicting this premise. E1 supports the BCC tendency and role of refractory elements, but does not demonstrate entropy dominance over enthalpy. E3 is irrelevant to the core mechanism.
premises: High configurational entropy at elevated temperatures suppresses enthalpically driven local ordering or clustering in HEAs.
The inclusion of high-melting refractory elements stabilizes a disordered single-phase (typically BCC) structure.
The dominant entropy stabilization overcomes chemical pair-interaction forces that would otherwise promote phase separation or ordering.
The predicted stable single-phase HEAs show a strong tendency to form BCC phases, linked to refractory elements and high melting points.
